question: Does the interleaving that regressed the adopted term reproduce when the transport is the production NetworkTransport over the real TCP stream layer rather than the in-process substitute stream layer the first check used, and can that path be exercised at all in this execution environment?
rationale: Exploration, not a fixed check, for the last recorded unknown on the term-context line: whether the substitute stream layer is what let the heartbeat callback run concurrently with the main goroutine, or whether the production transport behaves the same. The harness repeats the first check's interleaving verbatim - arm a StableStore wrapper, send a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries so that the real transport classifies it and invokes the registered callback on its connection goroutine, hold that callback's CurrentTerm write, send a higher-term AppendEntries through the main loop on a second connection, then release the held write and read the term context - with the only change being that both endpoints are NewTCPTransport instances over 127.0.0.1 and no substitute fabric exists. It skips when the TCP transport cannot bind, which is what happened in the local construction environment, so the output retained from the clean copy will show either the same regression over the production transport or that the transport was unavailable there; either way the exploration records which of the two premises remains open rather than assuming one. Because it is an exploration it creates no Evidence and does not touch the unit that the first check already completed, so a skipped run cannot disturb that record.
